items.stem: Why should a dbt model reference upstream models with `ref()` instead of a hard-coded table name?

options.text: ref() builds the dependency DAG and resolves the correct schema per environment
options.rationale: Correct: ref() lets dbt order builds and target the right environment schema.

options.text: ref() runs faster SQL at query time
options.rationale: ref() is about dependency resolution, not query speed.

options.text: ref() loads raw data into the warehouse
options.rationale: dbt transforms in-warehouse; ref() does not load data.

items.explanation: Correct: ref() lets dbt order builds and target the right environment schema.

items.stem: What is the risk of an incremental dbt model without a correct `unique_key`?

options.text: New runs can insert duplicate rows instead of updating existing ones
options.rationale: Correct: without a unique_key dbt cannot match and update rows, causing duplicates.

options.text: The model will refuse to compile
options.rationale: It compiles; the problem is runtime duplication.
Docs generation is independent of unique_key.

items.explanation: Correct: without a unique_key dbt cannot match and update rows, causing duplicates.
